metadata.description: Speak in one language, hear it in another. Streaming speech-to-speech translation with the translated text alongside the audio.

info.description:
**Endpoint:** `wss://fal.run/Kotoba-Technologies/kotoba-sts/v1/realtime_voice`

**Playground:** upload a clip at https://fal.ai/models/kotoba-technologies/kotoba-sts/v1/speech-to-speech to get the translated text and speech.

**Overview:** Stream microphone audio in and receive both the translated text and the
synthesized translated speech back on the same connection, with latency low enough for a live
conversation. Source and target languages are set when the session opens; one session
translates in one direction.

**Use cases**
- Cross-language meetings and customer support calls.
- Live interpretation for events, tours, and hospitality.
- Multilingual voice agents that answer in the caller's language.
- Real-time dubbing of live streams.

**Technical specifications**
- Transport: WebSocket, JSON events with base64 audio.
- Input audio: 16-bit PCM or float32; configurable sample rate. Recommended: 24 kHz, mono.
- Output: translated text deltas and translated speech (16-bit PCM, 24 kHz).
- Client: any WebSocket client, or the Kotoba Python SDK.
- Supported language pairs (● stable, ▲ beta; rows are the spoken language, set in
  `language`; columns are the translated output, set in `target_language`):

| Input \ Output | Japanese (`ja`) | English (`en`) | Korean (`ko`) | Mandarin Chinese (`zh`) |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **Japanese (`ja`)** | — | ● | ● | ▲ |
| **English (`en`)** | ● | — | ● | ● |
| **Korean (`ko`)** | ● | ● | — | ▲ |
| **Mandarin Chinese (`zh`)** | ▲ | ● | ▲ | — |

**Example input**
```json
{"type": "voice_session.update",
 "session": {"input_audio_format": "pcm16", "input_audio_sample_rate": 24000,
             "input_audio_transcription": {"language": "ja", "target_language": "en"},
             "turn_detection": false}}
{"type": "input_audio_buffer.append", "audio": "<base64 pcm16>"}
{"type": "input_audio_buffer.commit"}
```

**Example output**
```json
{"type": "voice_session.updated", "session": {...}}
{"type": "conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.text.delta", "delta": "Good morning."}
{"type": "conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.audio.delta", "delta": "<base64 pcm16 24 kHz>"}
{"type": "input_audio_buffer.committed"}
```

**Example (Python SDK)**
```python
import kotoba

STS = "wss://fal.run/Kotoba-Technologies/kotoba-sts/v1/realtime_voice"
client = kotoba.KotobaClient()

# File in, translated audio out
result = client.s2st.translate("meeting_ja.wav", src="ja", tgt="en", url=STS)
result.to_wav("meeting_en.wav")

```

Live microphone: send audio and play results concurrently, so translated speech starts while
the microphone is still open.

```python
import asyncio
import kotoba

STS = "wss://fal.run/Kotoba-Technologies/kotoba-sts/v1/realtime_voice"

async def main():
    client = kotoba.AsyncKotobaClient()
    async with client.s2st.stream(src="ja", tgt="en", url=STS) as session:

        async def feed():
            async for chunk in mic_chunks():  # PCM16 chunks from the microphone
                await session.send_audio(chunk)
            await session.commit()

        feeder = asyncio.create_task(feed())
        async for event in session:  # runs while audio is still being sent
            if event.type == "partial_transcript":
                print(event.text, end="", flush=True)
            elif event.type == "audio_chunk":
                await play(event.audio)
            elif event.type == "done":
                break
        feeder.cancel()

asyncio.run(main())
```

**Pricing:** $0.035 per minute of session (unit: second of session, $0.000583 per second).

## Using the Kotoba Python SDK

The `kotoba-sdk` package (PyPI, Python 3.10+, version 0.2.3 or newer) covers all four apps.
It sends the fal key with fal's `Authorization: Key` scheme automatically for `fal.run` URLs,
so use the fal key as the API key and point the per-route URLs at the apps.

```bash
pip install kotoba-sdk
export KOTOBA_API_KEY=<fal key>
export KOTOBA_ASR_REST_URL=https://fal.run/Kotoba-Technologies/kotoba-stt/v1
export KOTOBA_ASR_URL=wss://fal.run/Kotoba-Technologies/kotoba-streaming-stt/v1/realtime
export KOTOBA_TTS_URL=wss://fal.run/Kotoba-Technologies/kotoba-tts/v2/tts/ws
export KOTOBA_S2ST_URL=wss://fal.run/Kotoba-Technologies/kotoba-sts/v1/realtime_voice
```

An app that has been idle may boot a GPU runner on the first request, which can take a few
minutes. Allow for that in the request timeout or retry the first request; the SDK's default
timeouts are 30 seconds for HTTP requests (`KotobaClient(timeout=...)`) and 15 seconds for the
WebSocket handshake.

x-fal-metadata.about:
Kotoba STS translates speech into speech over a WebSocket connection. Stream audio in and receive the translated text and the translated speech on the same connection, with latency low enough for a live conversation. One session translates in one direction.

**Endpoint**

```text
wss://fal.run/Kotoba-Technologies/kotoba-sts/v1/realtime_voice
```

The [Playground](https://fal.ai/models/kotoba-technologies/kotoba-sts/v1/speech-to-speech) offers a one-shot demo (`POST /v1/speech-to-speech`) that translates one uploaded clip. It is bounded for demos. Production integrations use the WebSocket endpoint described below.

### Capabilities

- Live speech translation for meetings, customer support, interpretation and multilingual voice agents.
- Translated text and translated speech (16-bit PCM, 24 kHz, mono) while the speaker is still talking.
- Input as 16-bit or float32 PCM at any sample rate (resampled server-side), or 8 kHz mu-law for telephony.

### Supported language pairs

Every pair of the four languages is supported (●). Rows are the spoken language (`language`); columns are the translation (`target_language`).

| Input \ Output | Japanese (`ja`) | English (`en`) | Korean (`ko`) | Mandarin Chinese (`zh`) |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **Japanese (`ja`)** | — | ● | ● | ● |
| **English (`en`)** | ● | — | ● | ● |
| **Korean (`ko`)** | ● | ● | — | ● |
| **Mandarin Chinese (`zh`)** | ● | ● | ● | — |

### Open the session

Send JSON messages over the WebSocket. Open the session with one `voice_session.update` message, then wait for `voice_session.updated`, which echoes the applied settings.

```json
{
"type": "voice_session.update",
"session": {
  "input_audio_format": "pcm16",
  "input_audio_sample_rate": 24000,
  "input_audio_transcription": {"language": "ja", "target_language": "en"}
}
}
```

| Setting | Type and values | Default | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session.input_audio_transcription.language` | string: `"ja"`, `"en"`, `"ko"` or `"zh"` | required | Language spoken in the audio. |
| `session.input_audio_transcription.target_language` | string: `"ja"`, `"en"`, `"ko"` or `"zh"` | required | Language to translate into. See the pairs above. |
| `session.input_audio_format` | string: `"pcm16"`, `"float32"` or `"twilio"` | `"pcm16"` | `pcm16` and `float32` are raw little-endian samples; `twilio` is 8 kHz mu-law. |
| `session.input_audio_sample_rate` | integer | `24000` | Sample rate of the input. Other rates are resampled server-side; `twilio` is always 8000. |
| `session.input_audio_number_of_channels` | integer | `1` | Interleaved multi-channel input is mixed down to mono. |
| `session.turn_detection` | `false` | `false` | The session translates one continuous stream; there is no turn detection. |

Then send audio, base64-encoded:

```json
{"type": "input_audio_buffer.append", "audio": "<base64 PCM16>"}
```

### Receive the translation

Field values below are illustrative.

```json
{"type": "voice_session.updated", "session": {"...": "..."}}
{"type": "conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.text.delta", "item_id": "...", "delta": "Good morning."}
{"type": "conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.audio.delta", "item_id": "...", "delta": "<base64 PCM16, 24 kHz, mono>"}
{"type": "input_audio_buffer.committed"}
```

- `text.delta` carries the translated text. Concatenate the deltas; an empty delta carries nothing.
- `audio.delta` carries the translated speech as 16-bit PCM at 24 kHz, mono. Play or append it in order.

### Finish the session

Send a commit after the last audio:

```json
{"type": "input_audio_buffer.commit"}
```

The commit ends the session. The server translates the remaining audio, sends `input_audio_buffer.committed`, and closes the connection with code 1000 a few seconds later.

The translated speech trails the speaker by a few seconds. To keep the end of the translation, keep sending silence after the speaker stops until the translated speech has finished, then commit.

### Session limits and errors

- A session ends after 5 hours of connection time with `{"type": "error", "error": "session_sts_quota_exceeded"}`. Open a new session to continue.
- If the deployment has no free capacity, the WebSocket upgrade is refused with HTTP 503 (`system_busy`). Retry with backoff.
- Invalid settings return `{"error": {"type": "invalid_request_error", "code": "...", "message": "...", "param": "<field>"}}`. An unsupported language (`invalid_languages`) closes the connection; for other invalid settings, send a corrected `voice_session.update` on the same connection.
- Errors during the session arrive as `{"type": "error", "error": "<message>"}`.
- An idle app boots a GPU runner on the first connection, which can take a few minutes. Warm the app with `GET https://fal.run/Kotoba-Technologies/kotoba-sts/model_and_cuda_availability` (same `Authorization: Key` header) or allow for it in the first connection's timeout.

### Authentication

Authenticate the WebSocket upgrade with `Authorization: Key <FAL_KEY>`. Keep the fal key on your server; do not ship it to browsers or mobile clients.

### Using the Kotoba Python SDK

`kotoba-sdk` 0.3.2 or newer on PyPI talks to this endpoint and selects the `Key` scheme for `fal.run` hosts.

```bash
pip install "kotoba-sdk>=0.3.2"
export KOTOBA_API_KEY=<fal key>
export KOTOBA_S2ST_URL=wss://fal.run/Kotoba-Technologies/kotoba-sts/v1/realtime_voice
```

Live microphone: send audio and read results concurrently, so translated speech starts while the microphone is still open.

```python
import asyncio
from kotoba import AsyncKotobaClient

async def main():
  client = AsyncKotobaClient()
  async with client.s2st.stream(src="ja", tgt="en") as session:

      async def feed():
          async for chunk in mic_chunks():  # PCM16 chunks at 24 kHz from the microphone
              await session.send_audio(chunk)
          await session.commit()

      feeder = asyncio.create_task(feed())
      async for event in session:
          if event.type == "partial_transcript":  # translated text
              print(event.text, end="", flush=True)
          elif event.type == "audio_chunk":  # translated speech
              await play(event.audio)
          elif event.type == "done":
              break
      feeder.cancel()

asyncio.run(main())
```

`client.s2st.translate("meeting_ja.wav", src="ja", tgt="en")` translates a file and returns a result with `to_wav()`. It commits right after the file ends, so add a few seconds of silence to the end of the file to keep the last words.

### Pricing

Billing is per second of input audio sent on the session, silence included. See the model page for the current rate.
